title: Lunceford's band and battles of the bands
summary: Dance says Basie names Lunceford as another swinging band; Edison recalls battles of the bands and the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You know something funny, several times when I've been talking with Basie I've said, Well, okay, we know about your band swinging. What other band swings? And he always says the same thing. He always says Lunceford's.
Lunceford's band was a good band.

But he always says it. You know, when I'm trying to sort of define swing or something, he's always said, 'Oh, yeah, you know, people say this and that about it.' But he says, 'When they got in their thing, they could rock all night. It's different, an entirely different kind of band.

Yeah. But you know, they used to have a battle of the bands quite often, you know. And I remember once we had done so many one-nighters and Jimmy Lunceford, you know, he had such a disciplined band. They were all -- he was in the Cotton Club, you know. We never did have a chance to play in the Cotton Club, that nightclub. The only thing we did, Stanley, we'd do the Savoy sometimes for three weeks.
Were you in there when they went to the Grand Terrace?
